top_story: An apparent Iran-US understanding on 16 June to end fighting in Lebanon did not stabilize the crisis, as Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon continued and Tehran shifted from coercive warnings on 19 June to reclosing the Strait of Hormuz on 20 June. By 21 June, Iranian messaging had hardened into explicit conditions: Hormuz will stay shut until a Lebanon ceasefire holds and oil waivers are granted, tying regional de-escalation to both battlefield restraint and sanctions relief. This builds on a longer pattern set in March, when US threats against Iran’s power grid and Tehran’s vows of regional escalation made clear that Hormuz and Lebanon were being fused into one deterrence arena. The immediate effect is to widen the cost of the Lebanon war from the border zone to energy markets and civilian livelihoods across the region, with Israel’s campaign now carrying a direct risk of a broader Iran-US confrontation.
